name: Boris Johnson
role: UK Prime Minister (2019–2022); former Foreign Secretary, Mayor of London and MP
summary: Johnson is a Conservative who calls himself a one-nation Tory, mixing free-market, free-trade and Brexit-sovereignty positions with large state spending on the NHS and levelling up, and socially liberal stances on matters such as same-sex marriage. His record shifted over time: pro-immigration and sceptical on climate as Mayor, then a points-based, controlled immigration policy, net zero and nuclear expansion as Prime Minister, plus firm backing for Ukraine.

sources.title: Mayoralty of Boris Johnson
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Mayor of London record: London Living Wage, financial sector, policing

universal-healthcare.rationale: The manifesto he led calls the NHS 'free at the point of use' and based on need not ability to pay, and promises record cash funding.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The manifesto he led raised the National Living Wage target to two thirds of median earnings (about £10.50 by 2024) and widened it to everyone over 21.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: At the 2019 conference he praised 'dynamic free market capitalism' and told the CPS in 2021 he flew the flag for free markets, while also defending an interventionist state role in crises.

public-ownership.rationale: The 2019 manifesto says 'the railways need accountability, not nationalisation', and at conference he rejected Corbyn-style socialism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: At the 2021 conference he mocked Labour for 'taxing the rich till the pips squeak' and as Mayor he criticised the 50p rate; his government later raised National Insurance and corporation tax, and the manifesto promised limits on tax advantages for the wealthiest, so the evidence is mixed.

unions-good.rationale: He credited Thatcher with ending union restraints on trade, and the manifesto required minimum services in transport strikes, though it also said rail workers deserve a fair deal.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He described himself in 2011 as anti-regulation, but the 2019 manifesto promised stronger corporate governance, tougher pay and pension protections and more competition-regulator powers.

legalize-drugs.rationale: At the 2021 conference he attacked Labour for wanting to decriminalise hard drugs and promised to tackle drug dealers.

empower-police-military.rationale: His first act as PM was 20,000 more police, the manifesto backs stop and search, tasers and body cameras, and raises defence spending above inflation each year.

decide-locally.rationale: He argued the UK is the most centralised country, that 'Whitehall knows best' is over, and offered counties devolved powers and local leaders.

rehabilitation.rationale: The manifesto funds prison education and job coaches to cut reoffending, but pairs this with tougher sentences, more prison places and no automatic halfway release.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2012 as Mayor he urged the government to 'whack through' marriage equality legislation, saying he saw no reason to deny it.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: In 2020 he said Black Lives Matter protesters were right about discrimination and that government is committed to more work, but he stressed progress made and opposed unlawful protest.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: At the 2021 conference he said Conservatives will defend the country's history and cultural inheritance against cancel culture.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The 2019 manifesto says overall numbers will come down with fewer lower-skilled migrants, and at the 2021 conference he said the answer was to control immigration rather than use it to keep wages low.

free-trade.rationale: His Greenwich speech presents free trade as the economic idea that has done most to cut poverty and casts the UK as its global champion.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: As Foreign Secretary he criticised the West for setting red lines on Assad's treatment of civilians and then not acting: 'we willed the end, and failed to will the means'.

open-borders.rationale: In 2022 he rejected unlimited safe routes as 'open borders by the back door' and said Britain rejects it.

limit-growth.rationale: He argued the UK cut emissions by 42 per cent since 1990 while GDP grew about 70 per cent, presenting decarbonisation as compatible with growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He legislated net zero by 2050, announced the ten-point plan and a 2030 end to new petrol and diesel car sales, and hosted COP26.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: At the UN he said he was 'profoundly optimistic' about technology remaking the world 'wondrously and benignly' and rejected anti-scientific pessimism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: At Sizewell he said 'go nuclear and go large', pledging a reactor a year and at least eight new reactors.

central-planning.rationale: He rejected socialism and Venezuelan-style plans as 'deranged and ruinous' and said 'I am not a communist'.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He criticised mercantilists and protectionists waving tariffs 'like cudgels' and called for free trade with all.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His levelling-up speech says government must play a 'catalytic' strategic role and the manifesto pairs this with a large state infrastructure programme.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The manifesto calls home ownership one of the most fundamental Conservative values, giving people 'a tangible stake in society', and backs Right to Buy.

democracy-best.rationale: He called liberal democracy, the rule of law and free markets the 'great trinity of human progress' and said the British flag stands above all for democracy.

right-to-secede.rationale: As PM he refused a Section 30 order, saying he could not agree to any transfer of power that would lead to further independence referendums.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The manifesto describes 'modern Britain' as 'a diverse and tolerant country' and says society has been enriched by immigration.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He mocked Labour for 'levelling down' and races 'where nobody wins', and the manifesto stresses equality of opportunity.

algorithmic-government.rationale: At the UN he questioned whether machines alone should decide matters like mortgages or surgery and warned of digital authoritarianism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The manifesto he led says Labour 'detest the profit motive' and would destroy the basis of the economy, treating profit as a driver of national wealth.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The manifesto set strict limits on borrowing and said no borrowing for day-to-day spending, but in 2020 he defended borrowing to invest while costs were low and called for a 'New Deal'.

national-self-determination.rationale: He backed Ukraine's right to 'independence and national self-determination', though as PM he refused Scotland a further referendum.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The manifesto says people making the UK home should pay in for a reasonable period before accessing welfare, with EU arrivals getting benefits only after five years.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Everyone who can work should work is a general aim; no stated position on a work requirement for benefits.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The manifesto funds libraries and regional museums and he vowed to defend inherited culture at conference.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: In 2022 he noted more North Sea gas output, but the manifesto kept a fracking moratorium and he welcomed the prospect of a coal phase-out at COP26.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Integration language is nearby; no stated position on giving up original culture.

proportional-representation.rationale: The manifesto states the party 'will continue to support the First Past the Post system'.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Since the Brexit campaign he accused elites of cynicism and indifference to the suffering their policies caused.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The manifesto promised legislation against 'vexatious legal claims' that undermine the Armed Forces.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The manifesto promises that wherever people or their families come from, their rights will be respected with fairness and dignity, and his first speech cited equalities of race, gender and LGBT.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The manifesto he led commits to maintain a Right to Buy for all council tenants and to pilot new areas.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The manifesto promises to require a minimum service during transport strikes, saying unions should not undermine others' livelihoods.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The manifesto says the beliefs uniting Britons matter more than differences and that diversity and immigration have enriched society.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He led the Brexit campaign and as PM took the UK out of the EU to 'take back control' of laws, money and borders.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The manifesto pledges to bolster NATO, Five Eyes and other alliances and his government joined AUKUS (which he hailed in 2021) and doubled troops in Poland and Estonia.

death-penalty.rationale: Reported as saying he does not support the death penalty.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The manifesto proudly kept the 0.7 per cent of national income aid commitment, though his government cut it to 0.5 per cent in 2021.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The manifesto states 'we will maintain our Trident nuclear deterrent, which guarantees our security'.

collective-defense.rationale: The manifesto champions collective security and NATO alliance commitments and he reinforced allied frontline states in 2022.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: He called Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea an illegal land grab and condemned further annexations and sham referendums.

region-keeps-system.rationale: He said the G7 stands firm in upholding Hong Kong's way of life guaranteed by 'one country, two systems'.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He warned against 'bizarre autarkic rhetoric' and market segregation and argued for open exchange.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: A no-race-to-the-bottom pledge is nearby; no stated position on binding standards in trade agreements.

former-empire-influence.rationale: He wants to turn the Commonwealth into a free trade zone and said Brexit lets Britain reach out to its fastest growing economies.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The manifesto commits to legislate for animal sentience and tougher sentences for animal cruelty.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The manifesto ties farm support to high animal welfare standards and promises an end to excessively long live-animal journeys, while keeping farming and the Hunting Act unchanged.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: He said he did not believe in tearing down statues that are part of the national heritage and called attacks on monuments law-breaking, citing a Churchill statue.

non-intervention.rationale: He criticised the 2013 decision not to intervene in Syria after chemical weapons use and backed arming Ukraine against Russia's invasion.

national-law-over-international.rationale: In the UKIM Bill debate he said no British Prime Minister or Parliament could accept the country's boundaries being dictated by a foreign power or international organisation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: At the 2019 conference he said the NHS and public services depend on the growth from capitalism, which he said Conservatives should embrace rather than shun.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He told Holocaust Memorial Day that the Holocaust was the industrialised murder of 6 million Jews and pledged a national memorial so no one can doubt what happened.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: In 2022 his government excluded transgender people from the conversion therapy ban and he said trans women should not compete in women's sport or use women's changing rooms.

assisted-dying.rationale: Reported in 2024 as saying he would have voted against the assisted dying bill had he been given the chance.

islam-incompatible.rationale: As Foreign Secretary he said Muslims share the same hopes and values, and criticised the label Islamist terror as insulting to 1.5 billion Muslims; in 2018 he opposed a burqa ban though calling the garment ridiculous.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The manifesto commits to NATO and allied democracies and in 2022 he led deployments in support of NATO frontline states.

gm-crops.rationale: In 2019 he promised a bioscience sector 'liberated from anti genetic modification rules' with blight-resistant crops to feed the world.

future-generations.rationale: He tied COP26 and climate action to leaving a healthy planet for children and grandchildren and criticised short-termism harming future generations.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The manifesto states fiscal rules capping net investment at 3 per cent of GDP and requiring a reassessment if debt interest reaches 6 per cent of revenue.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The manifesto commits to keep the Trident deterrent as a guarantee of national security.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The manifesto promises tougher sentencing, an end to automatic halfway release for serious crimes and whole-life style terms for child murderers, though not general fixed sentences.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The manifesto prioritises a good grasp of English in the points system and boosts English teaching; in 2019 he said he wanted immigrants to learn English.

voter-id.rationale: The manifesto promised photo identification at polling stations and his government passed the Elections Act 2022 introducing it.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: He announced the UK joined 38 other countries referring Putin's actions to the International Criminal Court so he could not commit crimes with impunity.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: He cites the principle of self-determination for the Falkland Islanders, but condemned the 'sham referendums' in Russian-held Ukraine.

close-ties-china.rationale: He began as 'pro-China' in 2019 but by 2020-21 he offered Hong Kong residents a route to settle and joined AUKUS, turning more hawkish.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: He said BAME people do face discrimination in education, employment and criminal law, while also saying Britain is a much less racist society than before.

notes: Views changed: as Mayor (2008-16) he backed an amnesty for illegal migrants, same-sex marriage and wrote climate-sceptic columns; as PM (2019-22) he adopted net zero, a points-based system, the Rwanda policy and strong Ukraine support. Latest clear position used. Some Telegraph and Spectator columns, Hansard votes and his memoir 'Unleashed' were not available as full text, so answers rely mainly on his PM speeches, the 2019 manifesto and reference summaries.
